questions.traditionalCourse: Adult Health / Med-Surg II & Critical Care
questions.question: Which immediate action is appropriate for a fresh thermal burn after scene safety is established?
choices: Apply ice directly for 30 minutes
Stop the heat source, remove nonadherent hot items and jewelry, use cool running water when appropriate, and prevent hypothermia
Cover the burn with butter
Break every blister before assessment
questions.explanation: Initial care stops ongoing injury, removes constricting items before edema develops, cools safely without ice, and prevents hypothermia. Greasy remedies and routine blister disruption can cause harm.

questions.traditionalCourse: Adult Health / Med-Surg II & Critical Care
questions.question: Which statement about burn TBSA estimation is correct?
choices: Superficial erythema is included in resuscitation TBSA
Partial- and full-thickness areas are counted; superficial burns are not
The adult Rule of Nines is the most accurate method for infants
Burn depth and TBSA are the same measurement
questions.explanation: Resuscitation TBSA includes partial- and full-thickness injury, not superficial erythema. Depth describes tissue penetration, while TBSA describes area; children need age-adjusted proportions.

questions.traditionalCourse: Adult Health / Med-Surg II & Critical Care
questions.question: A patient from an enclosed-space fire has hoarseness, soot in the mouth, and increasing facial edema. What is the priority?
choices: Wait for stridor before calling for help
Obtain early expert airway assessment and prepare for intubation before edema progresses
Apply topical antibiotic to the face first
Encourage oral fluids and discharge
questions.explanation: Hoarseness, soot, enclosed-space exposure, and progressive edema suggest inhalation injury. Airway loss can evolve rapidly, and later intubation may become difficult; stridor is a late warning.

questions.traditionalCourse: Adult Health / Med-Surg II & Critical Care
questions.question: Why can a pulse oximeter reading of 99% be misleading after smoke inhalation?
choices: It measures only respiratory rate
Standard pulse oximetry cannot reliably distinguish oxyhemoglobin from carboxyhemoglobin
Carbon monoxide always lowers the displayed value to zero
Soot blocks every pulse-oximeter signal
questions.explanation: Standard pulse oximetry may display a reassuring saturation despite carbon monoxide poisoning. Give high-concentration oxygen when suspected and obtain co-oximetry without delaying treatment.

questions.traditionalCourse: Adult Health / Med-Surg II & Critical Care
questions.question: Which statement best describes the ABA adult burn-shock starting formula for burns at least 20% TBSA?
choices: 2 mL × kg × %TBSA estimates initial first-day crystalloid, but the rate must be titrated to response
The calculated total is a mandatory amount regardless of urine or lungs
4 mL × kg × superficial erythema is always required
The formula replaces hourly assessment
questions.explanation: Current ABA guidance recommends starting from 2 mL/kg/%TBSA for eligible adults to reduce excessive volume. It remains an initial estimate requiring hourly physiologic reassessment and specialist guidance.

questions.traditionalCourse: Adult Health / Med-Surg II & Critical Care
questions.question: A burn patient's urine output remains low while oxygen need, edema, and airway pressures rise during resuscitation. What is the safest response?
choices: Automatically double the fluid until urine output normalizes
Check catheter and perfusion, assess fluid responsiveness and compartment or organ complications, and urgently escalate the rising fluid requirement
Ignore the respiratory change because edema is expected
Stop all fluid without notifying the burn team
questions.explanation: Oliguria has multiple causes, and simultaneous congestion can indicate fluid creep or compartment physiology. The RN should reassess the whole patient and escalate rather than reflexively increasing or stopping fluid.

questions.traditionalCourse: Adult Health / Med-Surg II & Critical Care
questions.question: Which change in a circumferential full-thickness arm burn requires immediate escalation?
choices: Improving capillary refill and stable movement
Increasing pain, paresthesia, coolness, weakness, and loss of Doppler signal
Mild itching in healed skin
A stable dry dressing
questions.explanation: Progressive neurovascular compromise under rigid eschar threatens the limb and may require urgent decompression. A pulse can persist early, so serial pain, sensation, motion, temperature, refill, and Doppler findings matter.

questions.traditionalCourse: Adult Health / Med-Surg II & Critical Care
questions.question: What is the appropriate initial approach to most chemical skin burns?
choices: Neutralize every acid with an alkali
Protect staff, remove contaminated clothing, brush away appropriate dry chemicals, and irrigate copiously while identifying the agent
Apply an occlusive oil before removing clothing
Delay decontamination until the exact chemical formula is known
questions.explanation: Decontamination should begin promptly with staff protection. Dry material may need brushing away before water, and most skin exposures need copious irrigation; blind neutralization can generate heat.

questions.traditionalCourse: Adult Health / Med-Surg II & Critical Care
questions.question: Why can a small electrical entry wound still represent a major injury?
choices: Electrical energy damages only the epidermis
Deep muscle, nerve, vascular, cardiac, and renal injury may be much greater than the visible surface burn
Every low-voltage exposure causes full-thickness burns
Entry wounds prove there is no trauma from a fall
questions.explanation: Electrical current can injure deep tissues along its pathway and cause dysrhythmia, rhabdomyolysis, compartment syndrome, or associated trauma despite limited surface findings.

questions.traditionalCourse: Adult Health / Med-Surg II & Critical Care
questions.question: Which plan best supports long-term function after a major burn?
choices: Delay motion until every wound and graft has fully matured
Begin team-directed positioning, splinting, range of motion, mobility, nutrition, pain control, and psychosocial support early while protecting grafts
Use routine systemic antibiotics until all skin closes
Avoid discussing body image or trauma
questions.explanation: Burn rehabilitation begins early to limit edema, weakness, and contracture while honoring graft precautions. Nutrition, procedural pain control, mental health, and patient participation are part of functional recovery.
